user.title: Growatt Datalogger
user.description: Home Assistant will listen for your Growatt datalogger on this port. After setup, open your datalogger's network settings, turn off domain-name resolution, and point its server address at this machine's IP on the same port.

data_description.port: Growatt dataloggers use {port} by default. Only change this if something else on this machine already uses it.

error.port_in_use: Something else is already listening on that port.

abort.single_instance_allowed: Growatt Datalogger is already set up.

data.relay_enabled: Also forward to the Growatt cloud

data_description.include_unknown: Creates a disabled diagnostic sensor for every register this integration cannot name. Useful for adding support for a new inverter; noisy otherwise.
data_description.buffered_policy: Records the datalogger replays after an outage carry a past timestamp, so they are never written to live sensors. 'event' fires growatt_datalogger_buffered_record for automations to consume; 'ignore' discards them.
data_description.relay_enabled: Mirrors every packet to Growatt so ShinePhone keeps working. Off by default, because the point of this integration is that nothing has to leave your network. If Growatt becomes unreachable, Home Assistant takes over answering the datalogger so you never lose data.
data_description.relay_host: Only used when forwarding is enabled.
data_description.relay_port: Only used when forwarding is enabled.

profiles.title: Inverter profiles
profiles.description: A record states which Modbus registers it carries, so the right decoding is normally worked out for you. A few families cannot be told apart from the record alone — an off-grid SPF, and some SPH inverters behind a ShineWiFi-S, report a 0-based block whose registers mean something entirely different from Protocol II's. If Home Assistant has told you it could not identify an inverter, or the readings are wildly wrong (a boost temperature in the hundreds, a daily yield in the millions), pick the matching profile here. Leave it on automatic otherwise.

port_in_use.message: Could not listen on port {port}: {error}. Home Assistant will keep retrying.

read_register.name: Read register
read_register.description: Read a Modbus register from an inverter or a datalogger parameter, and return its value.

device_id.name: Device
device_id.description: The Growatt device to read from.

target.name: Target
target.description: Whether the register belongs to the inverter or to the datalogger itself.

end_register.name: End register
end_register.description: Read a contiguous range ending here. Inverter targets only.

write_register.name: Write register
write_register.description: Write a Modbus register. Register meanings vary by model and firmware; a wrong write can misconfigure the inverter, so anything outside a small allowlist needs Confirm.

device_id.name: Device
device_id.description: The Growatt device to write to.

target.name: Target
target.description: Whether the register belongs to the inverter or to the datalogger itself.

value.name: Value
value.description: A number for inverter registers, or text for datalogger parameters.

confirm.name: Confirm
confirm.description: Required for registers outside the known-safe list.

sync_time.name: Sync time
sync_time.description: Set the datalogger's clock to Home Assistant's local time.

device_id.name: Device
device_id.description: The datalogger whose clock to set.

adopt_history.name: Adopt history
adopt_history.description: Give a Growatt entity the entity ID of the sensor that used to read this inverter, so its history, its long-term statistics and everything pointing at it carry over. Delete the old integration first.

target_entity.name: Growatt entity
target_entity.description: The entity that should take over the old ID.

source_entity_id.name: Old entity ID
source_entity_id.description: The entity ID the previous integration used. It must no longer exist; its recorded history stays behind and is what gets adopted.

discard_target_statistics.name: Discard the Growatt entity's own statistics
discard_target_statistics.description: Delete the statistics this entity compiled under its old ID, which nothing can reach afterwards. They cover the period the old sensor was recording in parallel, so this normally loses nothing.

write_registers.name: Write registers
write_registers.description: Write a contiguous run of Modbus holding registers in a single operation. Use this when a value spans more than one register, or when several registers must change together: writing them one at a time leaves the inverter briefly holding a mix of old and new values.

device_id.name: Device
device_id.description: The Growatt inverter to write to.

start_register.name: Start register
start_register.description: The first register in the run.

values.name: Values
values.description: A list of 16-bit values, written to consecutive registers starting at the first.

confirm.name: Confirm
confirm.description: Always required. A multi-register write covers a range rather than one documented setting.

unconfident_profile.title: Could not identify Growatt inverter {serial}
unconfident_profile.description: The register layout reported by inverter {serial} does not match any family this integration knows, so its readings are being decoded as `{profile}` — a guess. If the values look right, you can ignore this. If they look wrong (a daily yield in the millions, a temperature in the hundreds), open the integration's options, choose **Inverter profiles**, and pin a profile for this inverter. Off-grid SPF models, and some SPH models behind a ShineWiFi-S, need the `offgrid` profile.
